payload.claim: Acceptance criterion 1 explicitly requires that while `main` runs `batch`, the SIGTERM handler in place is unchanged from the one `main` was called with, and the task notes prescribe a specific witness for it (replace `cli._batch` with a stub that records `signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM)` and assert it equals the pre-call handler). No such test exists in `tests/test_sigterm.py`: every test there drives only the `cell` command. So the `batch` branch of `main` could install or leave in place a SIGTERM handler change (e.g. ignoring SIGTERM before dispatch) and no test in this diff, nor any existing test in `tests/test_cli.py`, would notice. Inserting `signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)` before line 271's `return _batch(args, ledger, out_dir)` keeps the whole suite green while silently breaking that clause of criterion 1, and the `criteria` gate's report of '3 criteria witnessed at head' overstates coverage of criterion 1 because this clause of it has no witness at all.
